judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge made is correct. I re-derived all of it: problem 1's series sums 3/(1 - 2/5) = 5; problem 2's limit is 1/2 so the nth-term test gives divergence; problem 4 is geometric with a = 6 and r = -1/3, summing to 6/(4/3) = 9/2; problem 5's limit is 3/5; problem 6's limit is 0 with p = 1/2 < 1; problem 7's bounce series is 24*(3/4)/(1/4) = 72 ft after the first drop and 12 + 72 = 84 ft in total, matching the judge's figures exactly. Eight problems, all on the requested geometric / p-series / nth-term ideas, and the study guide does separate a necessary condition on the terms from a convergence test. What the judge did not do is open the delivered answer key's Quick Answers bank, and that bank has the confirmed relation-rendering defect. verify.json records two VERIFIED comparisons - id 3 is {"type":"compare", "expected": ">"} (p = 3 against 1) and id 6 is the same shape with '<' (p = 1/2 against 1) - and answer_key.pdf's bank prints '3. -' and '6. -, 0'. Problem 8 is the sheet's one genuine manual item and it prints '8. -' with the identical glyph. A grader scanning the bank cannot tell that problems 3 and 6 were machine-checked while problem 8 was never checked by anything; two of the three em dashes are false blanks. This is the same mechanism confirmed on curr-044: render_quick_answers.py::_fmt calls sympy.sympify on the string expected, sympify('>') raises, and the except branch returns '---' - the glyph reserved for manual-only ids. The final response even advertises that 'both p-versus-1 comparisons' were checked, which the artifact contradicts. answer_key_quality 4/4 is not supportable on that evidence. Two smaller gaps: several printed answer slots have no verify entry at all (1(a)'s a and r, 3(a)'s p, 4(a)'s a and r), and five written demands - 2(b) 'say in one sentence why that conclusion follows', 3(c), 5(c) 'say in one sentence why that is wrong', 6(c) 'Explain what inconclusive means', 7(a) 'Explain in one sentence where the 24 comes from' - carry no manual entry, though the sheet's directions box says 'A conclusion needs its reason attached'.

strengths_to_preserve: The two front-page models are the best concrete representation in this batch and they are load-bearing rather than decorative. Model A tabulates the running totals of 3 + 6/5 + 12/25 + ... (3, 4.2, 4.68, 4.872, 4.9488) against a dashed asymptote at 5, and Model B tabulates the harmonic partial sums at 1, 10, 100 and 1000 terms (1, 2.929, 5.187, 7.485). Both are then referenced by name: problem 1 is 'the series behind Model A' and problem 8 says 'Model B on the front page is that series'. The whole misconception the sheet targets - shrinking terms are not enough - is visible in the two tables before a single test is named.

Problem 7 turns the geometric sum into a physical count that students routinely get wrong: the bounce distances are 24*(3/4)^n because the ball goes up AND back down on every bounce, and the worksheet asks the student to 'Explain in one sentence where the 24 comes from' before summing. The 12 + 72 = 84 split is then verified as its own eval entry, so the 'add the original drop' step is bound rather than assumed.

The answer key opens with a 'How to grade this sheet' paragraph that names the three things every answer must contain (family, deciding parameter with its comparison to 1, conclusion as a consequence) and states that 'A correct diverges with no named test and no parameter earns nothing'. On a classification sheet that instruction does more for consistent marking than the answers themselves.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers.py::_fmt sympifies each string expected; sympify('>') and sympify('<') raise, and the except branch returns the em dash '---' that the same function uses for manual-only ids. The delivered bank therefore prints verified relations and unchecked open responses with the same glyph.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '3. -', '6. -, 0', '8. -' - problem 8 is the sheet's only {"type":"manual"} entry
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 58-61: sympify inside a try, except returning '---'; and line 71-72 returning '---' for manual-only ids

root_causes.description: Printed answer slots without entries, and written demands without manual companions. Problems 1(a), 3(a) and 4(a) each ask the student to write down a parameter (a and r, or p) with no verify entry, and five 'explain / say why' slots are folded inside machine-verified ids while only problem 8 is declared manual.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 1: '(a) Write down its first term a and its common ratio r' - verify.json id 1 is a single series entry with expected 5
worksheet.pdf problem 5(c): 'Say in one sentence why that is wrong for this a_n' - verify.json id 5 is a lone limit entry
worksheet.pdf directions: 'A conclusion needs its reason attached.'

root_causes.description: The page budget is computed from the author's own workspace_cm declarations, so inflating those declarations raises the ceiling instead of failing the gate. This sheet declares 19 cm, 16 cm, 16 cm and 14.5 cm of workspace for items whose answers are a single parameter, producing 7 pages for 8 problems inside an accepted range of 4-9. gate_log.txt warns about exactly this and the build still passes.
evidence: gate_log.txt line 92-94: 'Page budget (ws, letter): 8 problems, 153.6cm of content / ideal 7 page(s) - accepted range 4-9' plus the note 'the fix is a SHORTER BLOCK ... not a larger workspace_cm, which raises the ceiling without recovering the stranded space'
worksheet.pdf is 7 pages for 8 problems; the judge scored visual_and_print_quality 3 citing 'the seven-page student packet is highly spacious'

improvements.title: Verified '>' and '<' on problems 3 and 6 print as the same em dash as problem 8's manual item
improvements.proposed_change: Handle relations before sympify in scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt. Add an explicit branch that maps the strings '<', '>', '<=', '>=', '=' and '!=' to their LaTeX glyphs and returns them directly, so a verified compare prints as '$>$' rather than falling through to the exception path. Separately, stop using one glyph for two meanings: reserve '---' for manual-only ids and print '(see solution)' when a value genuinely cannot be rendered, so the bank never conflates 'checked' with 'nobody checked this'. This shares a mechanism with quick-answers-must-not-typeset-python-builtins and both should be fixed together.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture verify.json with a compare entry expected '>', a compare entry expected '<' and a manual-only id. Assert the rendered bank contains '$>$' and '$<$' on the first two rows and '---' on the third only. Today all three render '---' and the assertion fails.
improvements.expected_impact: Every compare-type answer in the corpus becomes visible to a grader, and the em dash regains a single unambiguous meaning: nothing machine-checked this row.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is a pre-sympify branch on a closed set of tokens; existing numeric and symbolic rows are untouched.

improvements.title: Problems 1(a), 3(a) and 4(a) print parameter answers with no verify entry
improvements.proposed_change: Require one entry per lettered part. On this sheet: id 1 needs entries binding a = 3 and r = 2/5, id 3 needs an entry binding p = 3, and id 4 needs entries binding a = 6 and r = -1/3. Those parameters are the graded content of a classification sheet - the sum is the consequence - so a bank that prints only '1. 5' and '4. 9/2' hides the answers the sheet actually assesses. Pair this with a demand-count gate that fails when a stem's lettered parts outnumber its entries.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a stem with '(a)', '(b)' and '(c)' markers and one entry under that id. The gate must fail with 'problem 1: 3 lettered parts, 1 entry'. Adding entries for (a) and (b) passes. The fixture passes today.
improvements.expected_impact: The parameter that decides each classification is verified and printed, so the bank matches what the sheet asks for rather than only its final consequence.
improvements.risk: Low. Detecting lettered markers in the tex source is reliable; an explicit per-id override covers parts that genuinely need no separate answer.

improvements.title: 19 cm and 16 cm workspaces on one-line classification items yield 7 pages for 8 problems
improvements.proposed_change: Cap workspace_cm against the work an item actually demands instead of trusting the declaration outright. Derive a per-entry-type ceiling (a compare or a single-parameter eval does not need 16 cm) and make page_budget.py fail, rather than merely note, when declared workspace exceeds that ceiling without a figure on the item. The gate log already prints the right advice - 'the fix is a SHORTER BLOCK ... not a larger workspace_cm, which raises the ceiling without recovering the stranded space' - so promote that note to an enforced rule for figureless items.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a verify.json with a figureless compare entry declaring workspace_cm 16. page_budget.py must exit non-zero naming the item and its type ceiling. Lowering the declaration to the ceiling passes, and a figure-bearing item at 16 cm keeps passing. Today the fixture only emits a NOTE and the build succeeds.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the loophole that let five of my ten cases ship visually sparse worksheets while passing the layout gate, which is the one dimension the judge repeatedly scored 3.
improvements.risk: Medium. Ceilings that are too tight would reintroduce the compression the budget model exists to prevent, so they must be generous and figure-aware, and the failure message must point at the block, not at the workspace.

case_summary: Conceptually the strongest concept-models sheet in my batch: two partial-sum tables on the front page (a convergent geometric series climbing to a dashed asymptote at 5, and the harmonic partial sums at 1/10/100/1000 terms) that problems 1 and 8 then refer to by name, so 'shrinking terms are not enough' is something the student sees before any test is named. All eight classifications and sums are correct - I re-derived 5, 9/2, 72 and 84 and the three limits - and the key opens with a grading rubric that demands family, parameter and conclusion. The defect the judge missed is in the delivered answer key: verify.json records two VERIFIED comparisons (id 3 expects '>', id 6 expects '<') and the Quick Answers bank prints them as '3. -' and '6. -, 0', the same em dash it prints for problem 8, the sheet's only genuine manual item. I traced the mechanism to render_quick_answers.py::_fmt, whose sympify call raises on a bare relation and falls through to the glyph reserved for unchecked rows - the confirmed curr-044 behaviour. Two further gaps: the parameters the sheet actually assesses (a and r on 1 and 4, p on 3) have no verify entries, and five 'say why / explain' slots carry no manual companion despite the directions box requiring a reason with every conclusion. The 7-page length for 8 problems traces to workspace_cm declarations of 19, 16, 16 and 14.5 cm on one-line items, which the page-budget gate accepts because it derives the budget from those same declarations.
